No concrete mathematical defect or substantial repair is required. The unrestricted original P16 remains open under the supplied assignment; its historical INCONCLUSIVE verdict is unchanged.

B. The continuous-coefficient argument establishes the claimed theorem for every p>2n. Multiplication of weak second derivatives by the continuous inverse Hermitian coefficients defines L_sigma:W^{2,p}→L^p without differentiating coefficients. The frozen symbols ξ_iξ_j/(1+a_0^{kl}ξ_kξ_l) satisfy the permitted multiplier hypothesis, including at zero. Constants can be made uniform over the compact ellipticity family by a finite covering and absorption argument. Freezing on sufficiently small charts absorbs coefficient oscillation. Cutoff commutators contain only first and zeroth derivatives; the stated mollifier interpolation, or the reconstruction's explicit finite-difference identity, absorbs the first derivatives. Thus ||v||_{W^{2,p}}≤C(||L_sv||_p+||v||_p), uniformly along the interpolation path.

The maximum-principle passage has the required regularity. Smooth annular approximation converges uniformly up to the boundary, while operator errors converge in L^{2n}, because p>2n. The smooth ABP bound therefore passes to W^{2,p}. On the tangent annulus, the exponential barrier satisfies L_sφ=e^{-k|y|²}(4k²a^{ij}y_i y_j−2k tr a)>0 for sufficiently large k. Comparison forces a positive inward derivative at a zero minimum of the C¹ function M−v, contradicting its vanishing gradient. The tangent ball can be chosen near a relative boundary point of the maximum set inside a coordinate chart. This proves the strong principle, the constant kernel of L_s and the trivial kernel of L_s−1.

The compactness contradiction gives a uniform inverse estimate for L_s−1. The smooth starting operator has index zero by elliptic deformation to a Laplacian minus one and is injective by the maximum principle. Neumann openness and compactness closedness establish invertibility throughout the path. Finally, L_sigma differs from L_sigma−1 by the compact inclusion W^{2,p}→L^p. Hence its index is zero; its one-dimensional kernel gives a one-dimensional range annihilator in L^{p'}. No rough adjoint theorem or generator core is assumed.

A. On a coordinate ball, put v=u+rho with dd^c rho≥omega and beta=omega−dd^c rho. Every actual bounded product is the finite sum of beta powers wedged with closed Bedford–Taylor powers of dd^c v. Radial regularizations decrease to the genuine bounded psh representative. Their complex Hessians converge uniformly on smaller balls, since dd^c v has continuous coefficients. Bedford–Taylor continuity applied separately to every degree consequently identifies the actual products with sigma's ordinary exterior powers. Only smooth forms multiply the Bedford–Taylor currents. The author's additional W^{2,p} regularity assertion also follows from the continuous local Euclidean Laplacian, constant-coefficient potential estimates and a harmonic remainder; canonical uniqueness identifies the resulting continuous representative.

Uniform positivity permits u+t h for both signs of sufficiently small t, and these remain bounded genuine omega-psh potentials. Their actual products equal (sigma+t dd^c h)^n, whose first variation is n dd^c h∧sigma^{n−1}. The induced continuous F_t has the same normalization scalar, so B_0(F_t)=B_0(F). The supporting inequality gives ∫(F_t−F)dnu≤0. The uniform expansion F_t−F=t tr_sigma(dd^c h)+O(t²), using both signs, forces every support to annihilate L_sigma.

The duality step is valid: q=1+1/(4n)<n/(n−1), and its conjugate p=4n+1 exceeds 2n. The original L^q bounds, smooth Sobolev density and Hölder duality extend stationarity to all W^{2,p} tests. Every support density therefore belongs to the same one-dimensional annihilator; mass one identifies them. Nonemptiness supplies an actual support. Monotonicity and the shift rule give the uniform-norm Lipschitz bound for B_0. Nearby supports have only the unique support at F as a possible limit, and the two supporting inequalities squeeze both signed difference quotients to −∫H dnu_F. Their compactness can also be justified entirely within the permitted foundations using the uniform L^q bounds and weak reflexive compactness. Thus no additional probability-compactness premise is necessary. This proves every continuous directional derivative, without a Fréchet conclusion.

C. The permitted zero-mean sphere Green kernel constructs a bounded continuous solution of dd^c v=(A−a)w. Its logarithmic singularity is uniformly integrable; its distributional Hessian is exactly the stated continuous form. Alternatively, the reconstruction's smooth zero-mean approximation converges through the smooth Sobolev inverse. Pullback produces an actual bounded genuine potential with sigma=Aw+b kappa>0. The bounded-product identification and block expansion give sigma^{k+1}=(k+1)Ab^k w∧kappa^k, establishing c_0(F)=1.

For an arbitrary smooth full-variable test h, the inverse block matrix gives L_sigma h=A^{-1}L_w^x h+b^{-1}L_kappa^y h. Integration against mu=(A/a)w⊗nu_kappa cancels A in the horizontal term, which vanishes by sphere Stokes for each vertical slice. The vertical term vanishes by smooth stationarity for each base point. Fubini therefore proves full-test stationarity. The candidate has a bounded density, and B's one-dimensional annihilator identifies it with an existing actual support. Consequently B_0(G)≤−∫(G−F)dmu for every continuous G. For k=1, Stokes gives nu_kappa=kappa; Gauduchon's theorem is used only for k≥2.

D. Write eta=|z|^{-2}dd^c|z|². It descends under dilation and is smooth and positive. With the specified normalization, (dd^c|z|²)^2=(2/pi²)dλ_4, so integration over 1≤|z|<2 yields ∫eta²=4 log 2. Thus kappa=(4 log 2)^{-1/2}eta. The identity s(s^{-1})''+2(s^{-1})'=0 proves dd^c kappa=0. Stokes then gives ∫L_kappa h kappa²=0, establishing nu_kappa=kappa². In logarithmic radial and angular coordinates, kappa²=dt⊗dS/(2pi²), with t=log|z|/log 2 modulo one.

The Hopf quotient is smoothly S³×S¹. Its permitted H²=0 calculation makes any hypothetical Kähler form exact, contradicting its positive square integral and Stokes. Restriction to a Y fiber excludes a Kähler metric on X. The background is genuinely nonclosed: db∧kappa is nonzero and cannot cancel the purely vertical component b d kappa.

Let m_f=∫f(tau)w. Since 0<m_f<1, A lies strictly between a−epsilon and a+epsilon, has mean a and is everywhere positive. Also 1≤b≤3, so exp(F)=3Ab² is continuous and strictly positive. The unique support is explicitly (A/a)w⊗kappa². Along a transverse equatorial path with tau=t≥0, put A_*=a−epsilon m_f. Then F(t)−F(0)=log(1+(epsilon/A_*)/log(e/t))+2log(1+t/2), bounded below by c/log(e/t). Distance is comparable to t. This proves the divergent Dini integral and failure of every positive Hölder exponent for F itself. The reference remains nonsingular zero.

E and proof comparison. The actual dependency graph is n1→n2, (n1,n2)→n3, (n1,n2,n3)→n4, (n1,n4)→n5, and (n1,…,n5)→n6. It is complete and acyclic. The author and reconstruction proofs agree on every essential implication. The reconstruction's additional details concerning uniform frozen constants, tangent-ball selection and sphere approximation justify existing steps; they do not replace a defective argument.

The supplied S07 text permits the claimed algebraic overlap comparison. In the nonsingular two-curve setting its residual operator, probability and adjoint become L_sigma=A^{-1}L_w+b^{-1}L_kappa, nu=(A/a)w⊗kappa, and T=sigma/(2ab). Directly, dd^c T=0, ∫omega∧T=1, and ∫dd^c h∧T=(1/2)∫L_sigma h dnu. This checks the overlap without importing S07's separately assumed singular framework or its envelope formulas. No publication priority is certified. A's Hessian antecedent is never established for arbitrary continuous F, and no two-support counterexample or unrestricted completion follows.
